title: Disillusion
text:
Where does the harsh road lead me

        through steps of costly warning?

        To leave scattered on the wind

        just complaints against time and fate.


        If I look back at my error and madness,

        chastening is no small reward,

        but how feeling tyrannizes

        when it drives understanding itself from reason!


        Let the will leave captivity,

        for free will must not idolize

        the most sensitive part of harms.


        The fates will decipher the mystery,

        and my warning will remain, freed

        from another's delirium, in disillusions.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the sonnet's moral vocabulary of chastening, will, fate, and disillusion.

title: To a Lady's Kiss
text:
Divine mouth filled with sweetness,

        happy the lip that kisses and touches you,

        for among all that exist there is no mouth so sweet,

        nor chain so fit to imprison me.


        Not the tasty honeycomb of the hive

        provokes such pleasure and softness,

        for sweetness is in you, and yours diminishes

        amber, carnation, and lily.


        But hidden inside the honey

        is the cruel sting with which you wound me,

        and no one sees this sign of life;


        tender mouth and hardened breast,

        no, nor ever among all women,

        a mouth so soft and a heart so worthy.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the kiss as honeyed chain with a hidden sting.

title: To the Court Bailiff Pedro Vergel
text:
The key to the bull-pen, since he was more skillful,

        they gave to good Vergel, and because he was a close

        kinsman of those he has beneath his hand,

        since this town takes him for a lead ox.


        Though in this matter of horns he is master

        and dean of the faculty,

        a young bull, enemy of his brother,

        threw him to the ground with sinister intent.


        But since men have never seen

        one horn pierced by another horn,

        and Vergel is well loved by bulls,


        though this time they saw him hard pressed,

        he came out safe and sound, thanks be to Christ:

        for Vergel is fated against horns.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the bullfighting and cuckold 'horns' satire around Vergel.

title: To the House of a Courtesan Where a Suitor Came to Live
text:
Here lived Chenca, that jewel

        expensive for her fittings; this room

        was the tomb of the sixth commandment

        and the galley where Love was a good buoy.


        By God, this room that supports her

        throws sparks of lust into the wind!

        Her boldness invented this trap

        to play man with stage machinery.


        From that window, the insolence

        of her hair affronted the east,

        and in this one her glance was a sword thrust.


        But, O cruel penance for both!

        today the house shelters a suitor,

        and the famous Chenca is married.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the house as bawdy stage, commandment-tomb, and comic punishment.

title: Whoever Is Fortunate Will Be Loved
editorial_note: The translation keeps the paradox of choosing unrewarded service over fortunate love.
